sources.title: NGSS MS-LS1-2: Develop and use a model to describe the function of a cell as a whole and ways the parts of cells contribute to the function
OpenStax Biology 2e, 15.4 RNA Processing in Eukaryotes (mitochondrial DNA)

note.text: A mitochondrion has two membranes. The outer one is smooth and wraps the whole organelle.
The inner membrane is where most ATP, the cell's energy-carrying molecule, is made.

steps.title: Cristae
steps.instruction: Draw the five folds poking into the middle.

note.text: The inner membrane folds into cristae. Folding packs far more membrane into a small space, so more ATP can be made.

steps.title: Matrix
steps.name: matrix
steps.instruction: Tap the matrix: the space inside the inner membrane.

mistakes.outer: That's the gap between the two membranes. The matrix is inside the inner membrane.

steps.insideDetailsMistake: That's inside a fold of the membrane. Tap the open space of the matrix.

note.text: The matrix is the fluid inside the inner membrane. Mitochondria even have their own DNA.

steps.title: Name the parts
steps.instruction: Pick the name for each numbered part.

targets.role: A fold of the inner membrane.

mistakes.Outer membrane: The outer membrane is smooth. These folds belong to the inner membrane: cristae.

steps.title: What it does
steps.question: What does a mitochondrion do for the cell?

options.text: It releases energy from food, using oxygen, to make ATP
options.feedback: Yes. This is cellular respiration. It also gives off carbon dioxide, the CO2 you breathe out.
That's photosynthesis, in chloroplasts. Mitochondria release energy from food.

options.text: It stores the cell's main DNA
options.feedback: The nucleus does that. Mitochondria make ATP.
Ribosomes build proteins. Mitochondria make ATP.

steps.title: Inputs and outputs
steps.question: Which gas do mitochondria use up, and which do they give off?

options.text: Use oxygen, give off carbon dioxide
options.feedback: Right. That's why you breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide.

options.text: Use carbon dioxide, give off oxygen
options.feedback: That's photosynthesis in plants. Respiration is the reverse.
Nitrogen isn't used. Mitochondria use oxygen and release carbon dioxide.
They need oxygen to release energy from food, and release carbon dioxide.
